- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, reduce subsequent forecast values by 5–15% to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast mean is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction by 2–5% per day.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, adjust forecast to align with recent sentiment trend rather than historical mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid forecasting below 60% of 14-day moving average unless sentiment strongly supports it.  
- If forecast is > 10% above recent 18-day high, flag for manual review — often indicates overfitting or lagged reaction.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.33) and price is trending, apply slight smoothing to forecast to avoid false momentum.
